title: Practice: Area of Triangle using Sine

questions.stem: Find the area of a triangle with sides 8 cm and 11 cm and an included angle of 40 degrees. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: Area = (1/2) x 8 x 11 x sin(40) = 44 x 0.6428 = 28.3 cm squared (1 d.p.). Forgetting the 1/2 would give 56.3.

questions.stem: Find the exact area of an equilateral triangle with side length 10 cm.
questions.explanation: Area = (1/2) x 10 x 10 x sin(60) = 50 x (sqrt(3)/2) = 25 sqrt(3) cm squared.

questions.stem: A triangle has an area of 24 cm squared. Two sides are 8 cm and x cm, with an included angle of 50 degrees. Find x to 1 decimal place.
A triangle has sides 6 cm and 10 cm with an included angle of 130 degrees. What is the area to 1 decimal place?
questions.explanation: Area = (1/2) x 6 x 10 x sin(130) = 30 x 0.7660 = 23.0 cm squared (1 d.p.). sin(130) = sin(50) = 0.766, which is positive, so the formula works for obtuse angles.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has sides 9 cm and 14 cm with an included angle of 70 degrees. What is its area to 1 decimal place?
questions.explanation: A parallelogram can be split into two triangles, or use the formula: Area = ab sin(C) = 9 x 14 x sin(70) = 126 x 0.9397 = 118.4... = 118.5 cm squared (1 d.p.). Note: no 1/2 for a parallelogram.
